failure_summary.description: The agent returned the poem’s title instead of completing the quoted line with the missing word.
Bare prompts listing two people were treated as asking for their relationship, rather than their salient shared association in the context.
Answers used a related but nonmatching form, such as an acronym instead of its expansion, a descriptive addition, a nickname, or an extra name initial.

patch.reasoning: Add guidance for the uncovered bare-list prompt pattern and for clues asking what an abbreviation stands for. The other answer-form mismatches fall under existing concise, canonical-answer rules, so adding another broad formatting rule would be duplicative.

edits.content: - When a prompt consists only of a pair or list of names, do not assume it asks for the relationship among them. Check the context for the salient shared association the prompt is likely eliciting—such as a country, place, organization, work, or category—and return that shared entity when best supported. Give a relationship only when the wording asks how the entities are related.

edits.target: - Use complementary passages to confirm or disambiguate an answer when helpful. Follow the requested format and retain any qualifiers necessary to the answer.
edits.content: - When a clue asks what an acronym or initialism stands for, or asks what feature it names, give its spelled-out canonical expansion rather than repeating the abbreviation. Use the abbreviation itself only when it is the requested answer.
